newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco companies support settlement proposal.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco companies support settlement proposal.

text.p: Five tobacco companies said Wednesday they believe the proposed settlement reached with state officials last month appropriately balances factors that should be considered in any determination to ban nicotine.
"We look forward to the opportunity to make the case for keeping intact the provisions of the proposed resolution as negotiated," the companies said in a statement.
The statement was issued after President Clinton said that language in the proposed settlement would place an unreasonable restriction on federal regulation of tobacco.
"The preservation of the rights of American adults to choose to use tobacco products is a central element of the proposed tobacco resolution," the companies said.

"The White House has repeatedly made clear that it is not in favor of prohibiting the use of tobacco products by adults and the concern over development of a substantial black market has been articulated by the Food and Drug Administration itself."

"We understand President Clinton's remarks today in light of these prior statements," the companies said. "The risk of creating a substantial black market in tobacco products should be a legitimate concern to all Americans for a variety of reasons," they added, concluding that last month's proposal best addressed these concerns.

The statement was issued by Phillip Morris Cos Inc., RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.'s R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. unit, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, Loews Corp.'s Lorillard Tobacco Co. and United States Tobacco Co., a unit of UST Inc.
